Establish the constitution for a Parking Fee Calculator, a deterministic Python command-line tool:
- Use Python 3.12+ with only the standard library at runtime; no third-party runtime dependencies. Dev tools (pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, bandit) are allowed.
- Follow modular architecture and separation of concerns: input parsing and validation, tariff definition, the fee calculation as a pure function with no I/O, and a thin command-line layer.
- The tariff (grace period, hourly rates, daily cap, any penalties) MUST be defined as data in one module, separate from the calculation function.
- Money MUST be whole rupees held as integers and durations MUST be whole seconds or minutes held as integers. Floats MUST NOT be used for money or durations anywhere, including parsing.
- Behaviour MUST be deterministic: the same input file yields byte-identical output. No randomness, no reading the system clock, no network calls; every ordering and rounding rule MUST be stated in the specification.
- Define the command-line contract explicitly: one input file path argument; JSON result on stdout; exit code 0 on success; exit code 2 on invalid input with a single-line error message on stderr; no stack traces for expected errors.
- Include explicit input validation and error handling; invalid input MUST never produce partial results.
- Identify measurable quality standards, enforced by an independent harness: ruff reports zero errors; bandit reports zero medium or high severity findings; all tests pass; line coverage of src/ is at least 90%; every acceptance criterion in the specification maps to at least one automated test.
- Never expose secrets in source code. No credentials, API keys or .env files are committed. The program MUST NOT use eval, exec, pickle or shell execution, and MUST read only the input file it is given.
- Prefer simple, maintainable solutions over unnecessary complexity.
- The tests/ and .harness/ directories are owned by the human engineer and are outside the scope of Spec Kit implementation tasks: generated task lists MUST NOT include tasks that create or modify them, although a task MAY reference them for traceability. During implementation and repair, the coding agent MUST implement application code in src/ only, and MUST NOT modify the specification, tests/ or .harness/; delete or weaken tests or assertions; lower thresholds; disable lint or security checks; or bypass mandatory harness gates. Recorded harness results MUST NOT be edited manually. Specification artifacts MAY be changed only through the Spec Kit commands (specify, clarify, plan, tasks), and every legitimate specification change MUST be recorded with its reason.
Set the ratification date and last-amended date to 2026-10-31 and the version to 1.0.0. Leave no TODO or placeholder tokens in the file. Do not add requirements beyond those listed.
